version 0.1.0; PROJECT spacetimes: Revision_Deflation: the results of the CJT effective action along the deflation clock

column4: the paired state along the clock (13 moments, two particles): at every moment the solution of the gap equation is a minimum of the CJT potential (Newton's method on the potential reproduces the iterated gap function to 7.7e-12; the minimum along the ray lies at s = 1 to 4.6e-7; the smallest eigenvalue of the second variation is positive), the critical temperature from the potential equals that of the linearized gap equation to 2.6e-12, and the condensation energy is within 15 per cent of -nu N(0) gap^2/4 wherever the gap is below 0.1 E_F. The condensation energy deepens monotonically, in weak coupling with twice the logarithmic slope of the gap (to within 0.1 per cent), and the coherence length of the pair shrinks: for the first particle from 25 to 1.0 in units of 1/k_F. At the last 5 moments of that particle the gap exceeds 0.1 E_F, and at the last one the coherence length has fallen to the distance 1/k_F between the particles: the deflation carries the paired state from overlapping pairs towards bound pairs
